what_happened.line: The town faces a new, unplanned DEP requirement to document operation-and-maintenance plans for privately-owned sewer systems tied into the town system.
The commission approved the FY26 fourth-quarter sewer billing commitment by roll call vote.
Crews using old hand-drawn tie cards have not resolved sewer lateral locations at a Wallace Park-area property or at 100 Laurel Lane.
The commission is weighing a drain layer's proposal to extend an existing line at 100 Laurel Lane instead of renting a locating device.
The commission decided to keep its meeting time at 6:00 p.m. rather than reverting to an alternating 6:00/7:00 p.m. schedule.

why_it_matters: The DEP mandate could require owners of privately-owned sewer systems connected to the town system to produce plans and ordinance information on a tight timeline, and it lands on the town with no advance planning.
The approved quarterly commitment is what sets sewer billing for ratepayers this period.
Two property owners are still without a confirmed sewer lateral location, which affects their connection and any repair or extension costs.
